Research background

The NLP research behind my applied LLM work: how meaning is represented, compared and retrieved.

My graduate research at IASBS focused on scoring semantic similarity between augmented sentence pairs, using autoencoders and a Siamese BERT architecture benchmarked against SBERT and Augmented SBERT baselines. It shaped how I think about embeddings and evaluation.

Today I apply that foundation to production-style LLM systems: RAG pipelines, MCP-based agents and Neo4j-backed semantic search.

Semantic Similarity & Scoring

Autoencoder and Siamese BERT models for scoring augmented sentence pairs on semantic textual similarity.

LLM Applications & Agents

Prompt engineering and optimization, RAG pipelines, and AI agent design (via LangChain, MCP).

Graph-Based Retrieval

Neo4j graph databases for semantic search in LLM applications.
